name: ANLI
desc: Tests whether a model can judge if one sentence follows from another, using examples deliberately written to trick strong models.

name: CommitmentBank (CB)
desc: Tests whether a model can tell how strongly a speaker believes a clause embedded in their sentence — for example, after 'I doubt that…'.

name: MultiNLI
desc: Tests whether a model can judge if one sentence follows from another across many kinds of writing — fiction, phone calls, government reports and more.

name: QNLI
desc: Tests whether a model can tell if a given sentence from Wikipedia actually contains the answer to a question.

name: RTE
desc: Tests whether a model can decide if a short news passage implies a hand-written statement; a small, old and surprisingly hard set.

name: SciTail
desc: Tests whether a model can decide if a sentence found on the web supports a statement taken from a school science exam.

name: SNLI
desc: Tests whether a model can tell if one sentence logically follows from, contradicts, or is unrelated to another, using short sentences about everyday photos.

name: BoolQ
desc: Tests whether a model can answer real yes/no questions people typed into Google, given a Wikipedia passage.

name: CoQA
sota_model: RoBERTa + AT + KD ensemble (Zhuiyi) / TR-MT (WeChat AI)
desc: Tests whether a model can answer a chain of questions about a passage, where each question depends on the earlier ones.

name: DROP
desc: Tests whether a model can read a paragraph and do simple arithmetic, counting or date comparison to answer a question.

name: MultiRC
desc: Tests whether a model can answer questions that need information from several sentences, where more than one option can be correct.

name: QuAC
desc: Tests whether a model can answer a student's questions about a Wikipedia article turn by turn, including saying when there is no answer.

name: RACE
desc: Tests reading comprehension using multiple-choice questions from English exams given to Chinese school students.

name: ReCoRD
desc: Tests whether a model can fill a missing name or place in a sentence about a news article, which needs some common sense.

name: SQuAD 2.0
desc: Tests whether a model can find the answer to a question in a Wikipedia paragraph, or recognise when the paragraph does not contain it.

name: Natural Questions
desc: Tests whether a model can answer real Google search questions from memory, without being shown any document.

name: TriviaQA
desc: Tests how many trivia-quiz questions a model can answer from the facts it memorised during training.

name: WebQuestions
desc: Tests whether a model can answer short factual questions mined from Google search suggestions, from memory alone.

name: ARC
desc: Tests whether a model can answer grade-school science exam questions; the Challenge split contains the ones simple word-matching cannot solve.

name: COPA
desc: Tests causal common sense: given a short statement, which of two alternatives is the more likely cause or effect.

name: HellaSwag
desc: Tests whether a model can pick the most sensible continuation of an everyday scene from four options written to fool it.

name: OpenBookQA
desc: Tests whether a model can combine a given science fact with everyday knowledge to answer a question.

name: PIQA
desc: Tests physical common sense: given an everyday goal, which of two near-identical instructions actually works in the real world.

name: Story Cloze
sota_model: Li et al. 2019 (as cited in GPT-3)
desc: Tests whether a model can choose the right ending for a short five-sentence story about everyday life.

name: Winograd Schema Challenge
desc: Tests whether a model can work out who a pronoun refers to in sentences where only common sense decides — 'it' in 'the trophy does not fit in the suitcase because it is too big'.

name: WinoGrande
desc: Tests whether a model can fill a blank in a sentence with the right of two people or objects, using common sense about the situation.

name: Children's Book Test
desc: Tests whether a model can fill a missing word in a sentence from a children's book after reading the twenty sentences before it.

name: enwik8
desc: Measures how well a model predicts raw Wikipedia text one character at a time, scored as bits per character; lower is better.

name: LAMBADA
desc: Tests whether a model can guess the last word of a passage from a novel when that word can only be predicted from the whole passage.

name: One Billion Word
desc: Measures how well a model predicts the next word in a billion words of shuffled news sentences, with no context between sentences.

name: Penn Treebank
desc: Measures how well a model predicts the next word in Wall Street Journal text that has been simplified to a 10,000-word vocabulary.

name: text8
desc: Measures how well a model predicts cleaned-up Wikipedia text (lower-case letters and spaces only) one character at a time.

name: WikiText-103
desc: Measures how well a model predicts the next word in Wikipedia articles (large version with long articles); lower perplexity is better.

name: WikiText-2
desc: Measures how well a model predicts the next word in Wikipedia articles (small version); lower perplexity means better prediction.

name: CoLA
desc: Tests whether a model can tell if a sentence is grammatically acceptable English, using examples from linguistics textbooks.

name: MRPC
desc: Tests whether a model can tell if two news sentences say the same thing in different words.

name: QQP
desc: Tests whether a model can tell if two questions asked on Quora are asking the same thing.

name: SST-2
desc: Tests whether a model can tell if a movie-review sentence is positive or negative.

name: STS-B
desc: Tests whether a model can rate how similar two sentences are in meaning, on a scale from 0 (unrelated) to 5 (identical).

name: WiC
desc: Tests whether a model can tell if the same word means the same thing in two different sentences — 'bed' of a river versus 'bed' you sleep in.

name: GLUE
sota_model: Vega v1 (JD Explore) · Turing ULR v6 (Microsoft)
desc: A collection of nine sentence-understanding tests (grammar, sentiment, paraphrase, similarity and inference) combined into one overall score.

name: SuperGLUE
desc: A harder collection of eight language-understanding tests (yes/no questions, cause and effect, word sense, coreference and more) with one overall score.

name: CNN / Daily Mail
desc: Tests whether a model can summarise a news article into a few bullet points, scored by overlap with the editor's own summary.

name: WMT Translation
sota: Fr→En 39.2 (GPT-3) · En→Fr 45.6 (Edunov 2018) · De→En 40.6 (GPT-3) · En→De 41.2 (Wang 2018) · Ro→En 39.9 (mBART) · En→Ro 38.5 (mBART)
desc: Tests how well a model translates news sentences between English and French, German or Romanian, scored by overlap with human translations.

name: GPT-3 synthetic tasks
desc: A set of made-up probe tasks — multi-digit arithmetic, unscrambling letters, SAT-style word analogies and spotting machine-written news — used to test learning from examples in the prompt.
